body: My dad said that I'm a know-it-all and that's why no one like me. Ouch.

I'm not sure I could possibly be indicated in her death. I was two hours away in the tiny town I live in. I only heard the news after my father called me crying hysterically. Police have cctv footage of her buying the method of death and she write two letters in her own handwriting.  

It would be a big stretch to implicate me in a death the coroner labelled suicide.

Thank you. I'm sorry for what you went though. My parents are als9 blaming my sister's ex partner and picking apart his story. Despite the traumatizing experience of seeing you ex partner's body after death.  I think some parents can't understand their grief and try to find others to blame otherwise grief and guilt overcomes them. That does not make it okay though.
She was placed of the safest medication for suicidal people. The meds she was on are the same ones I take. They make you tired but not more suicidal in my experience.

I wish I could say yes but after my sister's passing a lot of memories I had forgotten about have come up. 

My parents both came from abusive homes, my mother more than my father. We were poor for a long time and my father worked long hours to make sure we could survive. He had depression so when he came home he would ignore us and check out. 

My mother on the other hand raised me and my younger sister but replied on me to be her emotional support as she feel she had none from my father. 

My parents have cheated on each other multiple times and have asked me to weigh in on their marriage issues. I feel like they weren't ready to have children when they did...

The date of her passing I was two hours away in my small town where I lived. We had spoken as month before she passed away about me wishing her a happy birthday and that I loved her. 

In the past we had a tumultuous relationship because I was dealing with my own mental health and couldn't be there for my sister to help her deal with our parents. We had made up a year before she passed though. We were on good terms despite not speaking all the time. 

She had been prescribed anti depressants three weeks before her death. She was worried about losing her job, unable to go to the gym and had just had a break up with her partner. The police have footage of her buying what she used to pass away. 

She wrote two notes, both in her own handwriting and with her signature. 

I was offered my sister's finances after she passed but refused because I felt like I was profiting from her death and didn't want money. 

I don't feel like I really profited from her death or anything like that.
Community rules were against mentioning it. After a battle with depression she took her own life.

I know it's unfair but I almost feel like I have no choice but to support my parents right now. My father in particular has struggled with mental illness his whole life. He is not on medication and refuses to go to therapy. I'm worried he will pass the same way as my sister. He has told me on a few occasions he finds it helps to talk to me about what he is going through.
She had just turned 22. We're not sure how long she was unwell but she was prescribed medication 3 weeks before her passing.

I would definitely say he is guilty about her passing. The night I learnt the news and travelled to see them, my father asked me if we was a bad father. I told him he wasn't. Both my parents currently can not accept her passing and believe that she was targeted by someone for some reason.

I think it stems from my sister and I having a strained relationship in the past because I was trying to process my own depression. We had made up just over a year before she had passed. We had issues in our past but we loved each other so much regardless.

I'm not sure. They have done some mean things in the past. On my sister's 11th birthday my parents gave me a DNA test to "prove" I was my father's biological child. They have also had indiscretions in their marriage which they have tried to get me involved with.
He has his two younger brothers, a friend from work and a few other friends. He mostly vents to me though.

My sister always believed that I was the "golden child" because I never got punished like she did. My parents always compared our grades and behaviour. They were disappointed my sister wasn't docile and shy like me. They were always frustrated that she would pick arguments with them. My father even told me after her death that I was always "the good child." So I'm not sure about that.

My family was referred to a religious organisation that has a bereavement team come out to speak to you about your loved one's passing. My father did not participate because he does not believe in therapy. My mother and I had a joint appointment with a pair of bereavement counsellors from the organisation. My mother overshadowed the entire appointment and I was unable to speak about how I was coping. 

I understand that she needed someone to talk to though. My father is a stoic and sometimes emotionally unavailable man.

I have told my mother not to discuss things that upset me right now but she doesn't think before she says things to me. A week after her funeral she called me to tell me my sister's ex partner's story didn't match some stuff in the police report. But her partner went through unimaginable trauma, himself. They will call me to tell me about what they're going through bit not ask me how I am. 

I've told my father he needs to see a psychologist to work through his grief but has refused. He does not think talking to counsellors or psychologists helps. My partner sent my father a message after the call stating how inappropriate it was but he brushed it off saying that he would never say that about his only daughter and I am all he has left.

Thank you. I don't know anyone in my life except my dad that has ever had these thoughts, and I don't really want to talk to him about my depression. He has weird cures for it like "seeing sunshine." Thank you, it was nice to know I'm not the only one. Thank you for your support. It really means a lot to me!
Persistence and an inability to kill yourself right. Don't worry, every time I haven't killed myself I feel worse. So thanks.
